title: [CQ-R13b] Inherited local-runner test gaps
description:
Objective: close two test weaknesses that QA left on CQ-R13 for the hardening pass.

Split out of CQ-R13 (task-f4811a72) by architect-e4b7eee0 on 2026-10-30. It depends on CQ-R11e (task-001d8ab3) and CQ-R10d (task-90847011), the last planned editors of the two test files.

1. scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs, row H4 (qa-6fa5d758 on CQ-R08):
   - It uses Promise.withResolvers(), which needs Node 22+, so it fails under the WSL default /usr/local/bin/node 20.18.
   - Replace it with a manual resolver: `let finish; const late = new Promise(resolve => { finish = resolve; });`.
   - docs/DEVELOPMENT.md keeps 'Node.js 18+'.
2. scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs, row C5's 'close before EOF' (qa-952969be on CQ-R11c; details in comment-997358d583ff4f2b9c0f9c779df7172f on task-53daa94f):
   - It emits close synchronously, before HELLO and OBS are delivered, so check-session.mjs outcomeOf's `|| !s.ended` guard is never pinned.
   - Defer the close, e.g. setImmediate(() => proc.emit('close', 0, null)). The frames then parse first, and close 0 arrives with stdout still open.
   - The row must stay infra-failure, and must still kill the stop-after-settle mutant it was added for.

Deliverable: the two test edits only. Prove that the mutant is now killed:
- temporarily remove `|| !s.ended` from outcomeOf and watch the row fail;
- restore check-session.mjs byte-for-byte;
- record the runs in the step note, and never commit the mutant.

Out of scope:
- any runtime change;
- other rows;
- .moe edits.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs (on WSL: env -i with the nvm Node 24 PATH). Also run `/usr/local/bin/node --test --test-name-pattern='^H4 ' scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs` and report its exit code.
definitionOfDone: H4 no longer uses Promise.withResolvers, and it passes under the WSL default Node 20.18 (`/usr/local/bin/node --test --test-name-pattern='^H4 '`) as well as under Node 24. Shown by both runs' output.

C5's 'close before EOF' row delivers hello and the observation before close 0 arrives with stdout still open, and resolves infra-failure. With `|| !s.ended` temporarily removed from outcomeOf, the row fails, and check-session.mjs is restored unchanged afterwards. Shown by the recorded runs.
Only the two test files change.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs, row H4 (QA qa-6fa5d758 on CQ-R08). Edit the LANDED bytes: CQ-R10d is the last planned editor of this file and lands first, so re-read the row.

Replace `const late = Promise.withResolvers();` (~line 812) with a manual resolver:
  let finish;
  const late = new Promise(resolve => { finish = resolve; });
Then adapt its two uses:
- `answer: () => late.promise` becomes `answer: () => late`;
- `late.resolve({ content: [] })` becomes `finish({ content: [] })`.
Keep the comment `// too late: never written`. Change nothing else in the row.

Run both of these:
- `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" /usr/local/bin/node --test --test-name-pattern='^H4 ' scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs`. That binary is Node v20.18.0. Before this change the row fails with 'Promise.withResolvers is not a function', the only failure, as measured at planning.
- the same pattern under the nvm Node 24 bin.
Both must report H4 ok (pass 1, fail 0). Keep the two outputs for complete_task.

If the Node 20 run exposes any other Node 22+ API in H4, replace it the same minimal way and name it in the step note.

Error handling: the resolver keeps the row's semantics exactly. The late reply still resolves after SESSION_TIMEOUT and must never be written.

scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs, row C5's 'close before EOF' entry (QA qa-952969be, comment-997358d583ff4f2b9c0f9c779df7172f on task-53daa94f). Edit the LANDED bytes: CQ-R11e is the last planned editor, so re-read the C5 rows table.

Today the entry is:
  ['close before EOF', proc => { proc.send(HELLO, OBS); proc.emit('close', 0, null); }]
It emits close synchronously, before the PassThrough delivers the frames. So it is infra-failure through !s.opened, which masks outcomeOf's `|| !s.ended` guard.

Change it to defer the close:
  ['close before EOF', proc => { proc.send(HELLO, OBS); setImmediate(() => proc.emit('close', 0, null)); }]
The frames then parse first, and close 0 arrives while stdout is still open.
- The expected value stays the default ended('infra-failure').
- The per-row kills assertion stays [].
- Change no other row.

If step 3's mutant A survives (the frames were not yet delivered at close), defer instead with proc.stdout.once('data', () => setImmediate(() => proc.emit('close', 0, null))) and say so in the step note.

Run `node --test --test-name-pattern='^C5 ' scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs` (nvm Node 24, env -i). It must pass.

MUTATION PROOF, in a scratch copy and NEVER in the working tree.

The working tree is shared, and the wrapper lands every session exit. A mutant left in scripts/local-runner/check-session.mjs could be checkpoint-committed. Mutating a copy proves the same thing, and the original is never touched.

1. Build the copy.
   - Run S=$(mktemp -d), then `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$S"`. These are read-only git commands only.
   - Overlay this task's two edited test files: cp scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs "$S/scripts/tests/".
2. Control: `node --test --test-name-pattern='^C5 ' "$S/scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs"` passes.
3. Mutant A, the EOF guard. In "$S/scripts/local-runner/check-session.mjs", replace the exact text `if (s.failed || s.killed || !s.written || !s.ended) return 'infra-failure';` with `if (s.failed || s.killed || !s.written) return 'infra-failure';`.
   - Confirm the replacement happened: grep -c of the mutated line is 1.
   - Run C5. It must FAIL on the 'close before EOF' label, getting 'passed' instead of 'infra-failure'.
4. Mutant B, stop-after-settle, the mutant the row was added for. Restore A by re-extracting the file: `git show HEAD:scripts/local-runner/check-session.mjs > "$S/scripts/local-runner/check-session.mjs"`. Then replace `if (s.closing || s.settled) return;` with `if (s.closing) return;`.
   - Run C5. It must FAIL on the final kill-count assertion, at the 'close before EOF' index, with 1 instead of 0.
5. Clean up: rm -rf "$S".
6. Prove the working tree is untouched: `git diff --quiet -- scripts/local-runner/check-session.mjs` exits 0.

Record in the complete_step note, for each of the control, A, B and the git diff: the command, its exit code and the failing assertion's label or line.

Error handling: if the copy cannot be built (git archive fails), STOP and report it. Never fall back to mutating the working tree.

VERIFY ONCE, fresh.

1. `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="<nvm Node 24 bin>:/usr/bin:/bin" node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs` must exit 0. Its fresh command, exit code and output tail are complete_task's verification evidence.
2. Run `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" /usr/local/bin/node --test --test-name-pattern='^H4 ' scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs` and report its exit code, which must be 0.
3. `git diff --check -- scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs` is clean.
4. A read-only `git status --short` shows that this task changed only those two test files. No runtime file changed, and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md still says 'Node.js 18+'. Never revert, stash, `git add -A` or commit a peer's or pre-existing dirty path.

Error handling: fix a failing row in the test, never in a runtime file.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review. Read the two-hunk diff as an attacker:
- Did either edit weaken an assertion, change an expected value or drop a row?
- Does H4's late reply still arrive only after SESSION_TIMEOUT and stay unwritten?
- Does the deferred close leave a pending timer or an unhandled event after the test ends? setImmediate fires once; check the run for leaked handles or a slow exit.
- Do the mutation runs truly isolate one mutant each? A was restored from HEAD before B.
- Is the working tree's check-session.mjs byte-identical to HEAD?
- Would I be embarrassed if this shipped?
Fix any finding, then re-run step 4's commands fresh before complete_task.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Mutating check-session.mjs in place (as the description words it) versus in a git-archive scratch copy: the copy was chosen. The checkout is shared, and the wrappers land every session exit, so a crash mid-mutant could checkpoint-commit the mutant. The copy proves the same kill, and `git diff --quiet` proves the original untouched. This satisfies DoD 2's 'restored unchanged' without ever editing the file.
- Mutant B (stop-after-settle) is run too. The description requires that the deferred row still kills it: settle with closing false, then the late 'error' calls stop. Only the guard keeps a SIGKILL from following.
- One setImmediate (QA's suggestion) versus waiting for stdout's first 'data': the setImmediate goes first. Mutant A surviving is the signal to switch to the data-gated close.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Measured at planning: /usr/local/bin/node is v20.18.0, and H4 fails there ONLY on 'Promise.withResolvers is not a function' (bridge test line ~812). nvm has 18.20.8, 20.20.2, 22.23.4 and 24.21.0.
- In check-session.mjs:
  - outcomeOf's first guard is `if (s.failed || s.killed || !s.written || !s.ended)`;
  - stop() opens with `if (s.closing || s.settled) return;`.
- C5's loop asserts per-row kills, then emits a late 'error' on every proc and checks the kill counts after 1.1 s. That is what kills mutant B on the 'close before EOF' row, because close settles there without stdout end, so closing is still false.
- The local-runner tests use only node built-ins, so the archive copy needs no npm install.
planningNotes.risks:
- CQ-R10d and CQ-R11e land edits in these files first. Re-locate the rows by label, not by line number.
- If HEAD's check-session.mjs drifted from the strings quoted in step 3, find the equivalent guards and quote them in the note. If a guard is gone, report it.
- This plan is tests only. No runtime or docs file changes.
